title: Acceptance evaluation impossible for a landed item with no naming history when turn-gated control is off (no checkpointed sighting can be produced)
outcome: An item that landed without its implementer ever naming a source root can still be independently evaluated through a supported path: either a documented way to produce the required sighting with turn-gated control off, or evaluation against an explicitly named root revision. There must be no dead end.
acceptance: A note documents, from source, how a root session with turnGatedControl=false obtains an 'acknowledged capture under the claim' (a checkpointed turn of the claim's session focused on the item), and whether that is reachable today.

If it is unreachable, a fix lands, or a documented, supported alternative exists, so the evaluation of an item lacking naming history can proceed after naming a root, without bypassing evidence rules. Tests cover the formerly dead-ended path.
The full gate passes on the landed tree, with the review pair clean.
